title: Metals carry heat well through touch, and wood, plastic, and rubber do not
summary: Conduction is heat moving by direct touch. Metals such as copper and aluminum carry it well, and wood, plastic, and rubber carry it poorly.
body: OpenStax Physics says conduction is heat transfer through direct physical contact, as between a stove burner and the bottom of a pan. Some materials conduct thermal energy faster than others. In general, metals such as copper, aluminum, gold, and silver are good heat conductors, whereas wood, plastic, and rubber are poor ones. Convection, heat carried by a moving fluid, and the electrical kind of conduction are different cards. This one is only heat moving through a material you are touching.
